doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Members of the Catatonic Five
summary: Em Brown, Donny Andre, Johnny Johnson, Peter Ill and drummer Ronnie Zito, with Zito's later career.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I really don’t. And I bet you Donny Andre can tell you about that. And Dick Sherman will give you the history of jazz up to that point. But this was fall of ’55. And the band that came together was Em Brown, who was a senior, he was the clarinetist and the leader, Donny Andre was a sophomore and the banjo player and became the manager of the band and really did a yeoman job getting the gigs and doing all the hard work of running a band, and myself, a brand new trombonist just trying to learn how to play the trombone. We were the three Hamilton guys. And then Johnny Johnson — two guys from Colgate — Johnny Johnson who was a technically brilliant pianist from Colgate and went on to be a high school music teacher and Peter Ill who was a trumpet player from Colgate. And I don’t know what happened to Peter after he graduated. And then we always had remarkable drummers. And the two guys who played the most for us were Ronnie Zito — Ronnie was a young kid, probably 16, 15 from Utica, and he played with us a lot. He loved to go on these gigs, he loved my jokes, he just had the best time, and he was just a powerful drummer. He had the greatest time in the world. And he was supposed to go to Europe with us but his mother wouldn’t let him go. But Ronnie of course went on to become a famous drummer and made some great sides with Woody Herman, some of the I think some of his classics — “Opus de Funk,” the old Horace Silver tune with Ronnie Zito on drums. Just an unbelievable, powerful, big drummer.
